name: [research] WhatsApp Cloud API pricing, free tier, and Meta setup friction
description:
## Question

What does WhatsApp Business/Cloud API actually cost and demand in 2026 for a hobby-scale transactional notifier?

Resolve: current per-message pricing by category (utility/auth) for EU + Brazil; what is genuinely free today (service conversations, user-initiated window); per-message vs conversation pricing changes through 2024-2026; Meta Business verification burden + app review; template pre-approval process and turnaround; phone number requirements (dedicated number, can it be a virtual/eSIM?); BSP alternatives markup (Twilio, 360dialog, Meta direct). Output: cost table + friction list + verdict on 'free service messages' viability.
result: Resolved. Findings on throwaway branch research/whatsapp-pricing (a2d37ec), file docs/research/whatsapp-cloud-api-pricing-2026.md. Gist: NO genuinely free outbound path — server-initiated reminders are business-initiated and always require paid pre-approved templates: utility class ~EUR 0.0142/msg Portugal, ~EUR 0.0056 Brazil, ~EUR 0.0456 Germany. Free 24h-window service messages never applied to server-initiated sends and are removed Oct 1 2026 anyway. Setup friction: Meta Business verification (3-10 days, legal entity), non-VoIP dedicated number, template approval minutes-48h. BSPs only add cost at hobby volume (Twilio +$0.005/msg, 360dialog EUR 49/mo flat); Meta direct cheapest. Implication for strategy ADR: WhatsApp = paid channel only, candidate for premium gating.

name: Switch pickup sweep to Playtomic third-party API
description:
Replace the blocked api.playtomic.io integration (403 CloudFront from Fly datacenter IP) with the official third-party API at https://thirdparty.playtomic.io. Verified reachable from Fly (token endpoint returns 400, not 403).

Scope:
- Auth: POST /api/v1/oauth/token {client_id, secret} -> 1h Bearer token. Token cached, refresh on 401.
- Data: GET /api/v1/bookings?tenant_id=...&start_booking_date&end_booking_date&sport_id&status=PENDING&page&size. Returns real bookings: booking_start_date (UTC), booking_end_date, duration, resource_id/resource_name (court), sport_id, price, origin, participant_info. Paginate by page until fewer than size results (page-based, no metadata). Historical data kept 3 months.
- Sports: sport_id values PADEL TENNIS PICKLEBALL FOOTBALL7 FUTSAL FOOTBALL_OTHERS PADBOL SQUASH BADMINTON BEACH_TENNIS BEACH_VOLLEY BASKETBALL VOLLEYBALL CRICKET TABLE_TENNIS.
- Discovery: no club-search in this API. Need configured tenant list (PLAYTOMIC_TENANTS env: id+name+city). We know Porto/Lisbon clubs (e.g. CJD Padel Academy tenant 0cf889e9-...).
- Rework runPickupSweep: auth -> query PENDING bookings next 7 days per tenant -> create Open Pickups from real bookings (dateTime = booking_start_date, duration = booking duration). Drop the gap-inference heuristic / searchClubs path (or keep as fallback).
- No-op gracefully when creds absent (PLAYTOMIC_CLIENT_ID / PLAYTOMIC_SECRET unset) so nothing breaks.
- Rate limits: 400 req / 10 min. 429 -> retry with exponential backoff. Retry-After on payments 202.
- Deprecate src/lib/pickupSweep.ts detectBookedSlots + searchClubs/getAvailability in playtomic.server.ts if unused after switch.

BLOCKER: credentials. client_id+secret issued via Playtomic Connect partner program (playtomic.com/connect) or per-club Playtomic Manager Developer Tools. Request via Connect form; per-club creds only authorize that tenant.
result: Closed per request 2026-08-27: Playtomic third-party API sweep not planned, won't fix. GH will also auto-close on PR 869 merge via Closes #770.

name: Wear pull-to-refresh barely fills / requires repeated pulls; score screen silently no-ops for past-future games
description: Root causes: (1) pull-to-refresh nested-scroll consumed by TransformingLazyColumn + progress reset on finger-lift + 84dp/0.55 threshold needing ~153dp in one gesture. Fixed via PullToRefreshProgress (accumulates across gestures), onPreScroll read, 48dp/0.75 reachable threshold. (2) score 'start scoring' no-op for past/future games: ScoreViewModel observed today-scoped history but startGame records at event.dateTime (off-day invisible), no gating/reason. Fixed via observeLatestHistoryForEvent (event-scoped) + GameScorePhase gate (NOT_STARTED -> 'Starts in X' + 'Open teams'; ENDED -> 'Game over' + result). Verified: 13 new unit tests, 125 wear unit suite, DAO + E2E on WearOS5 emulator, live logcat prog=1.0 trigger.
result: Merged PR 866 (fix/wear-pull-refresh-score-gating d5585cb1 -> 7034c173 rebased onto f8c00b35, verified on main 07c3f8e2 bump). Fixes: PullToRefreshProgress 48dp/0.75 accumulates across gestures via onPreScroll (was 84dp/0.55 with reset-on-lift needing 153dp), verified logcat prog=1.0 trigger on Galaxy Watch4 SM-R870 + WearOS5. Score screen: observeLatestHistoryForEvent (was today-scoped, off-day invisible) + GameScorePhase gate NOT_STARTED->Starts in X+Open teams / ENDED->Game over+result. Tests: GameScorePhaseTest 8, PullToRefreshProgressTest 5, WearHistoryDaoTest off-day cases, ScoreUpdateE2ETest green, wear unit 125. Installed wear-debug.apk (51.6M) on 192.168.1.248:33143 SM-R870 API36. All 4 open MRs closed (825 stale, 785 MCP, 790 preview, 866 wear).

name: [wayfinder:map] Messaging channel strategy: Telegram-first, WhatsApp-later
description:
## Destination

A locked ADR deciding the messaging-channel strategy for Convocados notifications (Telegram now as a real free channel; WhatsApp later, possibly premium-gated), plus an implementation spec sharp enough to plan builds without re-deciding: schema, opt-in flows, dispatch wiring, phone capture.

## Notes

Domain: sports event notifications; existing channels are Resend email (default off), web push VAPID, FCM Android, in-app feed, webhooks. Dispatch: src/lib/notificationQueue.server.ts -> push.server.ts fanout; emails bypass queue. No User.phone field exists.
Consult skills: research (AFK tickets), prototype + grilling + domain-modeling (HITL). CONTEXT.md glossary governs terms (Follow, Tier 1/Tier 2, Invite).
Standing preferences: authenticated users only; brand stance compatible ('no chat chaos' = structured alerts fine); cost-sensitive — free channels first, paid only behind future premium feature.

## Decisions so far

- [[research] WhatsApp Cloud API pricing, free tier, and Meta setup friction]: No free outbound path — server-initiated reminders always need paid templates (~EUR 0.014/msg PT, ~EUR 0.006 BR); business verification + non-VoIP number required. Findings: branch research/whatsapp-pricing, docs/research/whatsapp-cloud-api-pricing-2026.md
- [[research] Telegram Bot API fitness for transactional game notifications]: Viable free third channel; opt-in Start deep-link binds chat_id to userId; best-effort delivery (403=opt-out); rich formatting + i18n; /unlink erasure path needed. Findings: branch research/telegram-fitness, docs/research/telegram-bot-api-fitness.md

## Not yet specified

- OTP/SMS verification provider choice (hangs on whether phone is verified now or at WhatsApp greenlight)
- Meta template approval workflow + message copy (only if WhatsApp greenlit)
- Per-channel failure/fallback policy (chat send fails -> email fallback? silent skip?)
- i18n of chat message copy across 6 locales
- Android parity sizing check for settings UI

## Out of scope

- Guest / anonymous EventPlayer messaging via SMS or WhatsApp (authenticated users only)
- Organizing games through WhatsApp group chats (brand stance)
- Changes to email or web-push channels themselves
result: Closed per request 2026-08-27: messaging channel strategy (Telegram-first) not planned, won't fix. GH will also auto-close on PR 869 merge via Closes #824.

name: iOS PWA: Google sign-in opens Safari; signin from event link lands on main page
description:
## Summary

On iOS Safari (both regular and as an installed PWA), signing in via Google from an event deep link (`/events/<id>`) does not return the user to the event. Two distinct symptoms:

1. **iOS PWA — Google sign-in opens Safari**: tapping "Sign in with Google" in the PWA triggers iOS's "Open in Safari?" sheet. The OAuth flow completes in Safari, not the PWA. The PWA never receives the session cookie, so every subsequent open shows the signin page again.

2. **Cross-browser — post-auth destination lands on `/` instead of `/events/<id>`**: after completing Google sign-in (in any browser), the user is redirected to the main page, not the event they came from. The `callbackURL` round-trip via the better-auth `state` cookie is being lost.

## Reproduction

### Setup
- iPhone with iOS 17+ (any browser; Safari standalone or as PWA from "Add to Home Screen")
- A public event link, e.g. `https://convocados.cabeda.dev/events/<id>`
- No existing session (clear PWA storage: Safari → Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → search "convocados" → swipe to delete; or reinstall the PWA)

### Steps
1. Open the event link
2. Tap **Sign in** in the header
3. On the signin page, tap **Sign in with Google**
4. Complete the Google auth

### Expected
- Step 3: Google auth opens in the PWA (or at least returns the user to the PWA after auth)
- Step 4: user is on `/events/<id>`

### Actual
- Step 3: iOS shows "Open in Safari?" sheet. The user signs in in Safari, not the PWA.
- Step 4: user is on `https://convocados.cabeda.dev/` (the main page), not the event.

### Firefox Mac (control)
- After the first signin, Firefox Mac stores the session cookie → subsequent visits skip the signin.
- Google sign-in does NOT open an external browser.
- The same `callbackURL` round-trip works correctly when the user is already authenticated (useEffect redirect), but after a fresh signin the redirect also lands on `/`.

## Root cause (hypothesis)

**Google sign-in on iOS PWA**:
- `signIn.social({provider: "google", callbackURL})` POSTs to `/api/auth/sign-in/social` from the PWA's context, which sets the `better-auth.state` cookie in the PWA's cookie jar.
- The client then does `window.location.href = <google-oauth-url>`. On iOS, this cross-origin navigation triggers the "Open in Safari?" sheet.
- The OAuth flow completes in Safari. Google redirects to `https://convocados.cabeda.dev/api/auth/callback/google?code=...&state=...`.
- Safari handles this. But the `better-auth.state` cookie is in the PWA's jar, not Safari's. The callback handler can't find the state → falls back to the baseURL redirect → user lands on `/` in Safari.

**Firefox / desktop Safari**: the same `state` cookie flow happens but the OAuth popup stays in the same browser context, so the cookie is available. The user reports it lands on `/` even in Firefox Mac, which suggests the `callbackURL` is not being preserved in the `state` cookie on this codebase's better-auth configuration, or the Google OAuth state encoding is broken.

## Investigation

A Playwright replication on **dev** (form signin path) confirms the form-based signin works correctly:
- `callbackURL` is correctly set in the URL
- Form `action="#"`, `method="post"` (ADR-0012 fix is live)
- React onSubmit intercepts the form, calls `/api/auth/sign-in/email`, then `window.location.href = postLoginURL`
- User lands on `/events/<id>` ✓

The Playwright test only covers the **form signin** path. The Google signin path (which the user is hitting on iOS) has NOT been tested end-to-end because it requires a real Google account and the full OAuth round-trip through `accounts.google.com`.

## Workaround

For iOS PWA users, the **form-based email/password signin** is the recommended path. It stays within the PWA and does not trigger the external browser sheet. The form signin is verified to land the user on the correct `callbackURL`.

## Proposed fix

1. **Short-term**: improve error handling on the signin page so that if the `callbackURL` is missing or the auth flow returns to a page without a usable destination, the user is shown a clear "where do you want to go?" picker instead of silently landing on `/`.

2. **iOS PWA Universal Links**: serve an AASA file at `https://convocados.cabeda.dev/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` that lists the OAuth callback paths. iOS will then route those URLs back into the PWA (or a future native iOS app) instead of opening Safari. Requires either a PWA with associated domains (not supported today) or a native iOS app (not in this repo).

3. **Better-auth state cookie hardening**: investigate whether the `callbackURL` is being correctly stored in the `state` cookie when `signIn.social` is called. If the cookie is being set with the wrong path (e.g., `/` instead of the full `callbackURL`), the post-callback redirect would fall through to the baseURL. This is a server-side better-auth configuration question.

## Environment

- Convocados v3.105.0 (post-ADR-0012 fix)
- iOS 17.x Safari
- Firefox 130+ on macOS
- PWA installed via "Add to Home Screen"

## Related

- ADR-0012: post-auth destination survives login
- Convocados-04z (fixed, deployed)
- PR #503 (fix), PR #505 (deploy)

## Priority

P1 — iOS PWA sign-in is the primary entry point for mobile users.
result: Popup-based Google sign-in shipped in PR #508; issue closed on GitHub. Marking dex task complete to match.

[research] Telegram Bot API fitness for transactional game notifications
description:
## Question

Can a Telegram bot serve as Convocados' third notification channel reliably and for free?

Resolve: Bot API basics for server-initiated DMs (sendMessage via chat_id — no template approval, no per-message cost, confirm still true 2026); rate limits (~30 msg/s global, per-chat caps); connect flow (user /start -> store chat_id; deep-link start payload binding to Convocados userId); delivery guarantees/reliability for time-critical reminders; policy constraints on transactional/notification bots; markdown/button support (inline keyboard = tap-through to event). Output: feasibility verdict + gotchas list.
result: Resolved. Findings on throwaway branch research/telegram-fitness (18e8042), file docs/research/telegram-bot-api-fitness.md. Gist: VIABLE free third notification channel. sendMessage via chat_id costs nothing, no templates/review; scale is ~5 orders of magnitude below the 30 msg/s ceiling. Hard constraint: bots cannot initiate — user must press Start via t.me/<bot>?start=<token> deep link (64-char payload) to bind chat_id to userId. Delivery best-effort: API acceptance != delivery receipt; blocked bot -> 403 (treat as opt-out), never-started -> 400; retry own 429s per retry_after. Richer than email: inline URL buttons (tap-through to event), HTML/MarkdownV2, per-user i18n via language_code. Policy clean for opt-in transactional bots; chat_id is personal data -> consent-on-Start plus /unlink erasure path required under Bot Developer Terms s4.

iOS PWA: Google sign-in via GIS ID-token (in-jar, no redirect)
description:
Installed iOS PWA has a separate cookie jar from Safari. Any Google OAuth flow that navigates to accounts.google.com (redirect OR popup) gets handed to Safari by iOS, so the session cookie lands in Safari's jar and the PWA stays logged out. Confirmed on-device: both popup (#508, reverted) and plain top-level redirect (#512) fail. Documented WebKit behavior, unchanged through iOS 17/18, no fix coming. FedCM unsupported on iOS Safari.

Fix: Google Identity Services (GIS) ID-token flow — never leave the PWA.
1. Load https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client; google.accounts.id.initialize({ client_id, callback }).
2. Render GIS button on iOS PWA (display-mode: standalone). Keep the existing redirect flow on all other platforms (works fine).
3. callback receives a Google ID token (JWT) in JS — no navigation.
4. authClient.signIn.social({ provider: 'google', idToken: { token } }) — better-auth verifies the JWT and sets its own SAME-ORIGIN session cookie -> lands in the PWA jar. (better-auth 1.6.19 supports idToken sign-in: 'If ID token is provided no redirection will happen.')
5. Keep email/password as fallback.

Expose client ID to the browser via a same-origin endpoint (GET /api/auth/google-client-id returning { clientId }) reusing existing GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID — mirrors the VAPID public-key pattern. Client ID is public.

MANUAL PREREQ (Google Cloud Console, OAuth client 45519759180-drrbd2j4sfa9dm2r0s1opmcgks9nb7qo): add to Authorized JavaScript origins: https://convocados.cabeda.dev, https://convocados.fly.dev, http://localhost:4321. GIS refuses to render otherwise. No new secret.

TDD. Detect standalone via matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches || navigator.standalone and prefer the idToken path there.

Refs: better-auth.com/docs/authentication/google ; developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/migration ; relates to #506.
